prOriginalConhecido.nota: Upstream calcom/cal.com now redirects to calcom/cal.diy. Found by head branch fix-collective-events-have-only-one-team-attendee-on-the-google-event-7754-cal-1267; benchmark head de62829 is the PR's last commit and squash c4e5d168 has the same 22-file diff (only unrelated main-merge drift in imports). Files later moved: EventManager -> packages/features/bookings/lib, CalendarManager -> packages/features/calendars/lib, handleNewBooking -> service/RegularBookingService + handleNewBooking/loadUsers.

tps.bug: When updateAllCalendarEvents fails before the calendar references are loaded, its catch now returns an empty array instead of a failed result, so a failed reschedule or location update looks successful to callers.
tps.evidenciaOpus: The catch block of updateAllCalendarEvents now returns calendarReference?.map(...) ?? [] (EventManager.ts:597-608). If the error is thrown before calendarReference is assigned (e.g. the newBooking lookup fails), the function returns an empty array, whereas before it returned a single success:false result. Callers that inspect the results therefore see no failure.
tps.evidenciaAstra: In packages/core/EventManager.ts:485, the awaited booking lookup can throw before calendarReference is assigned at line 495; the changed catch now returns [] at lines 597–607 instead of the previous failure result. A reschedule caller passes newBooking.id at packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1342 and treats empty results as the nonfailure branch at lines 1355–1361, hiding the failed calendar update.
